''' David Tong''' is a British [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]]. He is a professor at the [[University of Cambridge]], working in the [[Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics]] (DAMTP). He is also a fellow of [[Trinity College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/tong/|title = David Tong – Theoretical Physicist at the University of Cambridge}}</ref> His research mainly concerns [[quantum field theory]]. He is the joint recipient of the 2008 [[Adams Prize]]<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.maths.cam.ac.uk/adams-prize | title=List of Adams Prize Winners|date=28 December 2023}}</ref> and is currently a [[Simons Foundation#Simons Investigators awardees|Simons Investigator]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/mathematics-physical-sciences/simons-investigators/simons-investigators-awardees/|title=Simons Investigators|date=10 July 2018}}</ref> He is also known for his outreach activities and for his freely available lecture notes covering a wide range of topics in physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/tong/teaching.html|title = David Tong: Lectures on Theoretical Physics}}</ref>

==Research and career==
Tong grew up in  Crawley, UK. He attended [[Hazelwick School]] before undertaking his undergraduate studies in Mathematical Physics at the [[University of Nottingham]]. He completed his MSc in Mathematics at [[King's College London]], and his PhD in Theoretical Physics at [[Swansea University]].<ref name="www.damtp.cam.ac.uk">{{Cite web|url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/tong/bio.html|title=David Tong – Physicist – A Short Bio|website=www.damtp.cam.ac.uk|access-date=21 May 2019}}</ref>

He held research positions at the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (TIFR), Mumbai, at [[King's College London]] and at [[Columbia University]].<ref name="www.damtp.cam.ac.uk">{{Cite web|url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/tong/bio.html|title=David Tong – Physicist – A Short Bio|website=www.damtp.cam.ac.uk|access-date=21 May 2019}}</ref> Between 2001 and 2004 he was a Pappalardo Fellow at  [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] Center for Theoretical Physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://science.mit.edu/center-for-theoretical-physics-50-years/|title=Center for Theoretical Physics celebrates 50 years|website=MIT School of Science|language=en-US|access-date=30 December 2019}}</ref> He joined the faculty at Cambridge in 2004.

Tong works on quantum field theory and its application to different areas of physics. His early work was on [[Soliton|solitons]] and includes the discovery  (with Amihay Hanany) of a vortex solution in [[Supersymmetric Yang–Mills theory (disambiguation)|supersymmetric Yang-Mills theories]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hanany |first1=Amihay |last2=Tong |first2=David |last3=Tong |date=2003-06-17 |title=Vortices, Instantons and Branes |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |volume=0307 |issue=7 |page=037 |doi=10.1088/1126-6708/2003/07/037 |arxiv=hep-th/0306150|bibcode=2003JHEP...07..037H }}</ref> With [[Eva Silverstein]] and Mohsen Alishahia, he proposed a new, predictive mechanism for cosmic inflation based on the [[Born–Infeld model|Dirac–Born–Infeld (DBI) action]] which helped motivate more systematic analyses of primordial non-Gaussianity.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Alishahiha |first1=Mohsen |last2=Silverstein |first2=Eva |last3=Tong |first3=David |date=2004-04-13 |title=DBI in the Sky |journal=Physical Review D |volume=70 |issue=12 |article-number=123505 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.70.123505 |issn=1550-7998 |arxiv=hep-th/0404084 |s2cid=6632503 }}</ref> In work with Andreas Karch, he uncovered a web of dualities in 3d gauge theories.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Karch |first1=Andreas |last2=Tong |first2=David |last3=Tong |date=2016-06-06 |title=Particle-Vortex Duality from 3d Bosonization |journal=Physical Review X |volume=6 |issue=3 |article-number=031043|doi=10.1103/PhysRevX.6.031043 |arxiv=1606.01893 |bibcode=2016PhRvX...6c1043K }}</ref>

Tong is known for his widely watched videos on theoretical physics, including a [[Royal Institution]] lecture on quantum field theory,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zNVQfWC_evg|title=Quantum Fields: The Real Building Blocks of the Universe - with David Tong|website=[[YouTube]] |date=28 December 2023}}</ref> and a ''[[Quanta Magazine]]'' primer on the [[Standard Model]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Unl1jXFnzgo|title=The Standard Model of Particle Physics: A Triumph of Science|website=[[YouTube]] |date=28 December 2023}}</ref>

== Textbooks ==
David Tong has published books based on his theoretical physics lectures

* Volume 1: ''Classical Mechanics''
* Volume 2: ''Electromagnetism''
* Volume 3: ''Quantum Mechanics''
* Volume 4: ''Fluid Mechanics''
